name: Xteink X3 (4-level grayscale)
description: Xteink X3 driven in its 4-level grayscale mode rather than pure 1-bit mono. Same 792x528 panel mounted portrait (528x792 presentation) and the same CrossInk sleep-screen client as xteink_x3, but the server packs a 2-bpp buffer (104544 bytes) via esp32_gray2_bin and the firmware composites it as a base frame plus two grayscale planes. Pick this over xteink_x3 when the dashboard has photos or shading; stay on xteink_x3 for text and line art, where the extra levels buy little and the frame is half the size.
notes_md:
Awaiting confirmed test on real hardware. This entry exists because CrossInk's Tesserae client defaults to its grayscale build, which announces `xteink_x3_gray` on an X3; without a catalog entry under that id the device could never resolve its kind and pair, regardless of whether the grayscale path itself works.

Grayscale sibling of `xteink_x3`, mirroring the `xteink_x4_gray` pattern: same `esp32_bw_client` protocol and panel block as the mono entry, with the renderer overridden to `esp32_gray2_bin`.

Wire format is exactly 104544 bytes (792*528/4), 4 px/byte, MSB-first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white, linear. 792 is a multiple of 4, so the packer needs no row padding.

The renderer was written against UC8179-class panels, and the X3's controller family is different (UC8253, or UC8279d on later production runs). That difference should not matter to the wire format: the buffer carries no controller-specific data, and the firmware, not the server, expands it into the base frame and LSB/MSB planes that drive the panel. The X3-side plane composite is the same path CrossInk's own EPUB reader uses for 4-gray rendering on these controllers, including the OEM settle pass between the base frame and the planes that the X3 needs and the X4 does not. Expected to work, but inferred from the firmware source, not measured; treat the whole grayscale path as unverified until a frame renders on a real X3.

Orientation carries the same caveat as `xteink_x3`: `portrait_flipped` matches the hardware-verified X4 arrangement and the firmware draws both devices through the same framebuffer convention, but no X3 has rendered a frame yet. If a dashboard renders upside-down, switch to `portrait`.

Costs relative to `xteink_x3`: double the download per refresh, and three panel passes instead of one (base frame plus two planes), so a noticeably longer sleep-entry paint on a battery shared with an e-reader. Choose the mono entry for text and line art, this one for photos and shading.
